items.title: Pierre Boussaguet interviewed by Matthieu Jaffre, Aix en Provence, France, July 28, 2020
items.q: And I still had that concert to play with Griff.

ctx.x: He was too fragile to even — and I remember telling him it takes some guts. But of course, I said, “You know what? Forget about the saxophone. But why you don’t pass through the studio and say good-bye to your friends?” And then I said, “Why don’t you write a text, some poetry.” Because he was very gifted about that. And he said, “What kind of poetry?” I said, “Anything, a text, if you have something, and come to say hello to us.” And so he said, he called me back maybe ten or half an hour, he said, “I’ll be…

that piece of music, the ballad called “Charme.” Actually when I wrote the music, those weeks, I wanted to make a reunion of Guy Lafitte and Johnny Griffin. Because they knew each other since ever. But they never played together or just one concert, something like that. And then of course Guy got sick like early April I would say. And so, but I had written that ballad. The original title was “Griff and Guy.” Like Griffin and Guy. G and G. And then I asked Guy, with his beautiful poetry, which the text is a…
But he performed it very well. I mean we can really feel his emotions.
